question.problem:
Suppose that the function $f(x,y)$ and all of its first and second-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U.$ Find the values of $a$ and $b$, if 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =a{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+5{y}^{2}-3, \\ {f}_{y}(x,y) & =b{x}^{3}y+10xy, \\ {f}_{x}(2,1) & =14.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the mixed partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(a{x}^{2}{y}^{2}+5{y}^{2}-3) \\  & =2a{x}^{2}y+10y-0 \\  & =2a{x}^{2}y+10y \\ {f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(b{x}^{3}y+10xy) \\  & =3b{x}^{2}y+10y\end{aligned}
$$

Since the function and its first and second-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U,$ the mixed partial derivatives must be equal. Hence, we have the identity

$$
\begin{aligned}2a{x}^{2}y+10y & =3b{x}^{2}y+10y.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of ${x}^{2}y,$ we get $b=\frac{2}{3}a.$ 

Now, since ${f}_{x}(2,1)=14$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(2,1) & =14 \\ a(2)^{2}(1)^{2}+5(1)^{2}-3 & =14 \\ 4a+2 & =14 \\ a & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $b=\frac{2}{3}a=\frac{2}{3}(3)=2.$
